reviews.author: Sam B.
reviews.text: The camp host was super friendly and knowledgeable, dog access is a plus, and a ton of trails nearby. Plus, the road itself on the way up is very well maintained. Hope to stop by again soon!
Glad they reopened this campground - it's a nice quick escape from the city with plenty of accessible / semi accessible trails nearby. Sites are pretty basic, but have a bear locker.

Very clean campground with very nice tent pads. The bathrooms were spotless. A lot of great activities in the area: several trails. The only reason I gave 4 stars instead of 5 starts is because this campground is a little less than 1.5 hours from Seattle so you can sometimes get some "amateurs" from the city who have poor campsite etiquette. We were a couple sites down from one of two group sites and they were pretty noisy.

reviews.author: JAY M.
reviews.text: We had an amazing time here. The campground was quiet, not too crowded (Sunday - Tuesday) and so close to many trails. A quick walk to the river was a nice way to finish the day. We stayed in 17 and although it was near a road, it was private and you could not hear any road noise after the first hour or so. Restrooms were well maintained. Note: Water is currently unavailable. I'd come back.

I stayed here for three nights in site 11, which is very private and spacious. The vault toilet was very clean. There was a small black bear in my campsite one morning, but he was gathering berries and did not bother me or my belongings.

Loved our weekend at Middle Fork! We had one of the group campsites, and very easily fit 9 people. Toilets were very well maintained and the host was selling firewood. The river is only a five minute walk away, and we spent most of one day there. I was very surprised by how quiet it was for only being an hour outside of Seattle. The campground also had access to the CCC trail. The water pump was broken when we were there, so had to pack in all of our water.

We (family of 4) stayed here for two nights. Our 4 & 7 year old had a great time hiking the easy trails, fishing, exploring and chatting with other campers. Very close (1hr) to Seattle, but far enough to forget the city. Spaces were spread well, not cramped together. C.C.C. Trail access off the campground, fishing in Taylor or Snoqualmie. Great views of peaks, waterfalls, and for all-day hikes it's a great start point to various alpine lakes. We will come back when we can!

Spent one night here with a group. With so many campgrounds, I expected it to be very loud. It was not. Camp hosts were super nice and selling wood on-site. Pit toilets were surprisingly clean. We stayed at campsite 2. River a quarter mile walk away.

reviews.author: @TravisY5102975
reviews.text: I love this site due to its lack of cell reception and surplus of trees and greenery for the kids to explore. The river is a major plus too - it's close and manageable for fun rock and dam action. The site host was great and we enjoyed his hospitality. Actually looking forward to booking again soon!

reviews.author: @RobynS4454893
reviews.text: Cons: Too many deep potholes in the campground road. Too few birds. Did they migrate? Or don't they live in such a mono-agricultural environment? The drive in from town--the road's dangerously narrow. Especially for anyone towing a travel trailer or fifth wheel camper. The lack of plenty of pumped water was a shock. I saw the water spigot marked on the campground map before we set out for the site, and as a result I did not fill our camper's water supply before we arrived. That was not an expected outcome. There should be more power for the solar pumped well. And the spigot should have a 3/4 inch hose adapter on it. Or it should be made plain ahead of time that there is no water to fill a camper. The Vault toilets had terrible smells filling the air around and in the adjacent two or three campsites on both sides of them. The signs and rules discussing campfires in and around the campground were conflicting and ridiculous. We had no clue whether fires were forbidden everywhere, or if they were allowed within the campground, or they were only forbidden in dispersed camping. Only Upon Our departure did we run into the campground host who explained that we could have had a campfire every night. Thinking campfires were completely forbidden, we avoided them. And that was a big disappointment for everyone in our party. Pros: Beautiful deep forests of tall trees. Pacific Banana Slugs were COOL! Nice and quiet. Few campers present (it was the last week the park was open for the season). LOTS of hiking trails near beautiful rivers. Wonderful American Dippers and Vaux's Swifts and Red-breasted Sapsuckers. Excellent thick moss. Great signs explaining the historical impact of humans on Nature around us.

reviews.author: @CaitlinSE9CAFF
reviews.text: Super quiet during the week, definitely busier on the weekend. walkable to some trails and the river but would be easiest to drive if you have kids or want to picnic or anything.

reviews.author: @jimm7796384
reviews.text: Campground very clean and cared for. Campground Host very attentive with regular patrols. Restrooms always clean. Water supply needs and upgrade. One (1) water supply source is weak. Solar powered electric pump is not adequate for a CG of this size. Especially on a weekend.

reviews.author: @NicoleB2196888
reviews.text: This is the most beautiful campsite I have been to. The land is well cared for, the host is very helpful, the restrooms are clean enough, and the bear boxes are useful. I loved the access to trails and having a whole gorgeous forest right behind our tent. I wish our spot had been more private, but that was my only qualm.

reviews.author: @OleksiiMD5BBDA
reviews.text: Great location close to Seattle, but far from major highways. Very quiet, a lot of hiking trails around. Available wood from the host ($10/bundle), dog friendly, restrooms are in good condition. We come here every year and like it!

reviews.author: @BobH2675616
reviews.text: People who are prepared for what it offers, or actually doesnt offer, can and should have a wonderful time. It is very remote at the end of a narrow paved scenic 12 mile drive along the middle fork of the river. The beauty and quiet are worth the escape from modern city life. No cell service or electric hookups, pit toilets, fires allowed within their rings, and wonderful cold well water. It is well maintained with attentive and observant on site campground hosts. Have a great time.

reviews.author: @LorenR8BEAF424
reviews.text: The site aren't near the water!

reviews.author: @TracyM8497497
reviews.text: I reserved to spot for 6 people and 2 cars, when I arrived the space was small, only able to accommodate a single tent. We turned around and went home.

reviews.author: @TerryC3713393
reviews.text: Site 9 was excellent, the tent platform was flat hard packed level sand, tons of shade and the privacy of this campsite is wonderful. The host does a good job, the bathrooms are very clean and well stocked. I even had a deer walk straight to me and nibble on my shoe! Bring Off/Deet, the mosquitos are....friendly.

reviews.author: @RachelL4774006
reviews.text: This was my second time staying in Middle Fork Campground and we enjoyed it a lot. We stayed in site 17, which was nice and shaded, and the bathrooms and dumpsters were a good distance away. Everything was nice and clean and the pit toilets were always stocked with toilet paper and werent too stinky. The tent pad was nicely raked for our arrival and I didnt see any trash. Its a beautiful place to stay. Tons of wild flowers, and I especially enjoyed how many wild berries were growing around the campground as well. Im sure well be back again. :)

reviews.author: @TylerA5DB1F15F
reviews.text: Great camping spot. Right next to the bathrooms, trash cans, and near the water. I was worried we'd be able to smell some of it, but it was never an issue. Site 15 also has a trail that runs behind it - there's a makeshift path near the fire pit that connects to it. Take a left once you get to the trail, and you'll end up near the suspension bridge entrance. Super short walk compared to going out the campground entrance. No signal with Google Fi.

reviews.author: @HunterE82E644E
reviews.text: Incredible location with solid access to multiple hiking trails within a 30 minute drive. Being close to Issaquah is also very helpful for restocking supplies. The campgrounds were spacious and heavily forested with a walkable trail connecting the sites and leading directly to a hike. There were wild raspberry bushes scattered across our site. Would be mindful of the large amount of Foxglove that grows along the trails, and at some of the campsites, as its heavily toxic when ingested. So be mindful of small pets or young kiddos.

reviews.author: @JohnS6889697
reviews.text: This campsite is such a gem. Easy to get to, but you really feel off-grid because of how far out it is. The site was very well maintained during our stay, and Ian, the camp host was awesome! There is so much to do in the area - tons of beautiful trails, hiking, backpacking, biking, rafting and kayaking, fishing. Highly recommend. This campsite is going to be one of our yearly staples.

reviews.author: Hydroherr
reviews.text: Very private sites. Water and great trails everywhere. Only have gravity flush toilets but very clean. I recommend hiking to the top of Mount Si.

reviews.author: camper-693436
reviews.text: Great site, but very far out with no cell service.

reviews.author: Jason
reviews.text: Hidden Gem! This Campground was closed for several years, so it's just now becoming popular again. It's about 11 miles off of the freeway down a looooong narrow paved road following Middle Fork River. We're able to maneuver our 18' travel trailer into most spots pretty easily. Tons of trails and such for the kids and fam to explore. Taylor river is a short walking distance from the campground. Absolutely no cell service, but that's okay! I'd suggest making reservations, but you can usually find a spot if you get there early enough on the weekend.
